title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with activity as nations align under the Artemis Accords and the Space Force expands its launch capabilities. Meanwhile, funding and partnerships continue to shape the landscape, with significant developments in satellite production and tactical collaborations.

themes.title: Artemis Accords Expansion
themes.body: Mauritius has joined the growing list of nations signing the Artemis Accords, now at 70. This reflects a broader trend of international cooperation in lunar exploration, albeit with varying levels of commitment.

themes.title: Space Force Budget Boost
themes.body: The Space Force is tripling its launch contract ceiling, indicating a robust demand for satellite launches. Coupled with a $1.4 billion increase in the FY27 budget for space resilience, it seems the military is gearing up for a busy few years.

themes.title: Private Sector Moves
themes.body: Skyroot Aerospace has successfully reached orbit with its Vikram-1 launch, marking a notable achievement in the commercial space sector. Meanwhile, True Anomaly's $190 million Series C funding round highlights investor confidence in the burgeoning space domain awareness market.

themes.title: Defense Tech Developments
themes.body: Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN ground station program underscores the increasing reliance on data and analytics in defense. Additionally, the collaboration between Anduril and L3Harris for a tactical SDA constellation bid signals a shift towards integrated defense solutions.
